# What FoxPrivacy changes

<!-- Generated by tools/gen-docs.sh from policies/features.conf. Do not edit. -->

Every setting, what it costs, and the exact policy or preference behind it.

## How these are applied

Most settings are [Firefox enterprise policies][policies]. Their names are
checked against Firefox's own `policies-schema.json` by the test suite, because
a policy key Firefox does not recognise is ignored without any error a user
would ever see.

The rest are preferences, applied through the `Preferences` policy. Firefox only
accepts preferences whose names match an allowlist in its source, so those are
checked too.

Preferences are applied with `Status: default`, which means FoxPrivacy changes
the default value and a value you set by hand still wins. If you once turned one
of these on deliberately, FoxPrivacy will not turn it back off. That is the
intent: this project sets defaults, it does not override your decisions.

## Profiles

`standard` is the default. Nothing in it should be noticeable except the absence
of ads and nags. `strict` is standard plus everything in the second table, and
each of those has a cost worth reading first.

## Standard profile

| Feature | What it does | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| `telemetry` | Stops Firefox collecting and sending usage, performance, and health data to Mozilla. | Nothing you would notice. |
| `studies` | Stops Shield and Normandy silently enabling experimental features on your browser. | Nothing you would notice. |
| `crash-reports` | Stops crash reports being submitted automatically. The crash reporter still works; it just stops sending without asking. | Nothing you would notice. |
| `sponsored-content` | Removes paid placements from the new tab page: sponsored shortcuts, sponsored stories, and Mozilla's promotional snippets. | Nothing you would notice. |
| `firefox-suggest` | Stops what you type in the address bar being sent to Mozilla for online suggestions, and removes sponsored results from the dropdown. | Nothing you would notice. |
| `in-product-messaging` | Removes What's New pages, feature and extension recommendations, address bar interventions, More from Mozilla, and the onboarding tour. | Nothing you would notice. |
| `terms-of-use` | Skips the terms of use and data preferences screen newer Firefox versions show on first run. | Nothing you would notice. |
| `feedback-commands` | Removes the Submit Feedback and Report Deceptive Site menu items, which post data to Mozilla and Google. | You cannot report a phishing site from the menu. |
| `default-browser-agent` | Disables the scheduled Windows task that reports your default browser choice to Mozilla. No effect on Linux or macOS. | Nothing you would notice. |
| `ai-features` | Turns off the AI chatbot sidebar, link previews, smart tab groups, and smart windows. | Nothing you would notice. |
| `network-prediction` | Stops Firefox resolving, connecting to, and fetching pages you have not asked for. | Nothing you would notice. |
| `global-privacy-control` | Sends the Global Privacy Control signal, a legally recognised do-not-sell-my-data request in some jurisdictions. | Nothing you would notice. |
| `tracking-protection` | Keeps tracking protection on and adds cryptominer, fingerprinter, and email tracker blocking. Left unlocked so you can still make a per-site exception. | Nothing you would notice. |
| `home-stories` | Removes the recommended articles section, not just the sponsored entries in it. That section is fetched from Mozilla every time you open a tab. | The new tab page shows only your own shortcuts. |
| `search-suggestions` | Stops every keystroke in the address bar being sent to your search engine before you press Enter. A mistyped password reaches the engine without you ever submitting it. | No suggestion dropdown while typing a search. |
| `urlbar-trending` | Stops Firefox contacting your search engine the moment you click the address bar, before you have typed anything. | The address bar no longer offers trending searches when you click it. |
| `urlbar-speculative-connect` | Stops Firefox opening a connection to a guessed destination while you are still typing. NetworkPrediction does not cover this one. | Nothing you would notice. |
| `urlbar-single-word-lookup` | Stops Firefox turning a single word you type into a www.word.com request before searching for it. | A single word goes to your search engine instead of being tried as a hostname first. |
| `remote-improvements` | Stops Mozilla switching features on and off in your browser between updates through Nimbus rollouts. | Nothing you would notice. |
| `visual-search` | Turns off visual search, which sends an image from the page to a search provider. | No right click search by image. |

### Standard profile, policies and preferences used

| Feature | Keys |
|---|---|
| `telemetry` | `DisableTelemetry` |
| `studies` | `DisableFirefoxStudies` |
| `crash-reports` | `browser.crashReports.unsubmittedCheck.enabled`, `browser.crashReports.unsubmittedCheck.autoSubmit2` |
| `sponsored-content` | `FirefoxHome.SponsoredTopSites`, `FirefoxHome.SponsoredStories`, `FirefoxHome.Snippets` |
| `firefox-suggest` | `FirefoxSuggest.WebSuggestions`, `FirefoxSuggest.SponsoredSuggestions`, `FirefoxSuggest.ImproveSuggest` |
| `in-product-messaging` | `UserMessaging.WhatsNew`, `UserMessaging.ExtensionRecommendations`, `UserMessaging.FeatureRecommendations`, `UserMessaging.UrlbarInterventions`, `UserMessaging.MoreFromMozilla`, `UserMessaging.FirefoxLabs`, `UserMessaging.SkipOnboarding` |
| `terms-of-use` | `SkipTermsOfUse` |
| `feedback-commands` | `DisableFeedbackCommands` |
| `default-browser-agent` | `DisableDefaultBrowserAgent` |
| `ai-features` | `GenerativeAI.Chatbot`, `GenerativeAI.LinkPreviews`, `GenerativeAI.TabGroups`, `GenerativeAI.SmartWindow`, `GenerativeAI.Locked` |
| `network-prediction` | `NetworkPrediction`, `network.prefetch-next` |
| `global-privacy-control` | `privacy.globalprivacycontrol.enabled` |
| `tracking-protection` | `EnableTrackingProtection.Value`, `EnableTrackingProtection.Cryptomining`, `EnableTrackingProtection.Fingerprinting`, `EnableTrackingProtection.EmailTracking`, `EnableTrackingProtection.Locked` |
| `home-stories` | `FirefoxHome.Stories` |
| `search-suggestions` | `SearchSuggestEnabled` |
| `urlbar-trending` | `browser.urlbar.suggest.trending`, `browser.urlbar.trending.featureGate` |
| `urlbar-speculative-connect` | `browser.urlbar.speculativeConnect.enabled` |
| `urlbar-single-word-lookup` | `browser.fixup.alternate.enabled` |
| `remote-improvements` | `DisableRemoteImprovements` |
| `visual-search` | `VisualSearchEnabled` |

## Strict profile adds

| Feature | What it does | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| `captive-portal` | Stops Firefox periodically contacting detectportal.firefox.com to check for a login page. | Public WiFi login pages may not open by themselves. You may have to visit an http site to trigger them. |
| `strict-tracking` | Moves Enhanced Tracking Protection from the standard category to strict. | Some embedded logins, comment widgets, and video players need a per-site exception. |
| `fingerprinting-protection` | Enables Firefox's targeted fingerprinting protection, which limits the values scripts can read to identify your machine. | A small number of sites misdetect your browser or screen size. |
| `form-autofill` | Turns off storing and autofilling addresses and payment cards. | You type addresses and card numbers by hand. Saved passwords are not affected. |
| `referrer-trimming` | Sends only the site name, not the full page address, when you follow a link to another site. | A few sites that inspect the full referring URL may misbehave. |
| `webrtc-local-ip` | Stops video call code discovering your machine's local network addresses. Calls still work; this is not a WebRTC kill switch. | Some calls take longer to connect, or fail on unusual network setups. |
| `https-only` | Makes Firefox use HTTPS everywhere and warn before falling back to unencrypted HTTP. | Sites that are still HTTP only show a warning you have to click through. |

### Strict profile additions, policies and preferences used

| Feature | Keys |
|---|---|
| `captive-portal` | `CaptivePortal` |
| `strict-tracking` | `EnableTrackingProtection.Category` |
| `fingerprinting-protection` | `privacy.fingerprintingProtection` |
| `form-autofill` | `AutofillAddressEnabled`, `AutofillCreditCardEnabled` |
| `referrer-trimming` | `network.http.referer.XOriginTrimmingPolicy` |
| `webrtc-local-ip` | `media.peerconnection.ice.default_address_only` |
| `https-only` | `HttpsOnlyMode` |

## What is deliberately not here

App updates, Firefox Sync, the password manager, DNS-over-HTTPS, and Encrypted
Client Hello are left alone on purpose, and the test suite asserts that they
stay that way. The reasoning is in [VISION.md](VISION.md#what-is-deliberately-left-alone).

## Checking what is actually in effect

```sh
install/foxprivacy.sh --list      # every feature and its cost
install/foxprivacy.sh --verify    # is the file still installed and unmodified
```

Then restart Firefox and open `about:policies`. The Errors tab must be empty.
The Active tab shows what Firefox actually accepted, which is the only thing
that counts.

[policies]: https://firefox-admin-docs.mozilla.org/reference/policies/
